## You will be able to

- Apply OWASP LLM Top 10 controls
- Defend against direct and indirect prompt injection
- Enforce ACLs in retrieval and agents
- Red-team AI systems

## Demos

| # | Demo | Module | Min | Shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `01_threat_model.py` | 1 | 25 | a system described as components and data flows, mapped to LLM-specific threats with likelihood × impact scoring and the control that addresses each |
| 2 | `02_implement_five_controls.py` | 2 | 30 | eight attacks run against the system with controls switched on one at a time, showing which control stops which attack and what gets through with none |
| 3 | `03_red_team_exercise.py` | 3 | 25 | an automated probe of 16 attack variants against two configurations, scored into a findings report with severity, reproduction and recommended fix |
| 4 | `04_security_gates_and_metrics.py` | 4 | 15 | security checkpoints mapped to delivery gates, a release blocked by an open high finding, and five security metrics for the monthly report |

## Run of show
**One week before:** `python demos/run_all.py` on the laptop you will present from — it must print `ALL DEMOS OK`. Swap `demos/data/` for the client's own examples where you can. Print `exercises.md` per table and the handout per person.
**In the room:** each demo is one command from this folder: `python demos/NN_name.py`. No internet or API key needed. Each ends with a *Say it* line — your closing sentence.
**Live mode:** set `LLM_PROVIDER` and a key in the repo `.env`; demos that benefit then call a real model.
**In the browser:** every demo also runs from the `/demos` page (section *Course labs*) — useful for sales calls and the website.
